History:
• 33-year-old woman presents via tele-consult for sudden, new-onset left-sided headache that began ~4 h ago.  
• Onset: abrupt; first episode of this type.  
• Location/intensity: left hemicranium, behind/around eye; rated 6/10 (kidney-stone pain=10).  
• Associated symptoms: blurred vision with “zig-zag” lines (visual aura), dizziness, photophobia (cannot tolerate screens), nausea with two episodes of vomiting. Symptoms worsen with head movement; prefers lying still.  
• Relieving/aggravating: Paracetamol taken once 3 h ago (dose/route/frequency not documented) – no relief.  
• No limb weakness, speech disturbance, gait abnormality, or other focal neurological deficits.  
• Denies prior similar headaches.  
• Pregnancy thought unlikely.

Past Medical History:
• Kidney stones (remote).  
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Family history: mother—migraine and hypothyroidism.  
• Medications: none routinely; paracetamol earlier today (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Surgical/hospitalization history: not recorded.  
• Social history (tobacco, alcohol, drugs): not recorded.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-visit; no hands-on exam)  
• General: alert, conversant, oriented.  
• Neurological: patient reports normal strength and gait, no facial droop, speech intact.  
• HEENT, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, skin: not recorded.  
• Vital signs: not recorded.

Impression:
Likely migraine with visual aura presenting for the first time.  
DDx consistent with transcript:  
1. Migraine with aura – unilateral headache, visual phenomena, nausea/vomiting, positive family history.  
2. Sudden-onset secondary causes (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage) less likely given moderate pain and lack of neuro deficits but cannot be fully excluded without exam ‑ patient to be seen in person today.

Management Plan:
• Trial symptomatic therapy:  
  – Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) plus over-the-counter anti-sickness medication.  
  – Encourage oral fluids, especially sugary/carbonated drink (e.g., cola).  
• Arrange same-day in-person appointment for full neurological examination; patient to cancel if fully recovered beforehand.  
• Safety-netting: attend A&E/ED or call GP urgently if headache worsens, pain reaches “worst ever,” develops neck stiffness, confusion, weakness, speech or visual deterioration, or persistent vomiting.  
• Educate on migraine triggers and variability of age of onset.  
• No driving or operating machinery until symptoms resolve.

Patient Summary:
Maria, 33, with no headache history, developed an abrupt unilateral headache with visual aura, nausea/vomiting, and photophobia. Presentation most consistent with first-episode migraine; secondary causes judged less likely but will be evaluated at same-day clinic. Started on NSAID plus antiemetic and advised on red-flag symptoms.

Key Takeaways:
• Take ibuprofen with an anti-sickness tablet and a sugary fizzy drink as first-line relief.  
• Seek immediate care if pain escalates, new neurological symptoms appear, or no improvement before scheduled assessment.

Next Steps:
• Attend scheduled face-to-face appointment today for neurological exam; cancel only if completely symptom-free.  
• Consider escalation to specific migraine therapy (e.g., triptan) if inadequate response, to be discussed at visit.  
• Document vitals, perform fundoscopic and neuro exam, and consider urgent neuro-imaging if red flags emerge.
